newsitem.title: USA: U.S. beef producers told not to fear NAFTA growth.
newsitem.headline: U.S. beef producers told not to fear NAFTA growth.

text.p: U.S. beef producers have little to fear if the North American Free Trade Agreement is expanded to include Argentina and Chile, U.S. House Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith said.

"Frankly, they can't compete with our meat and our meat products," Smith, who has just returned from a tour of the two countries, told the National Cattlemen's Beef Association annual convention here.
He noted Argentina was an exporter of beef but could not match the tenderness of U.S. supplies as its cattle were fattened on grass over a longer period of time.
"The equivalent sirloin, T-bone steak or even New York cut is very, very tough," Smith said.
Chile imports 30 percent of its beef, mainly from Argentina, and its lack of quality differentiation was proving a barrier to U.S. supplies, he said.
"Our beef can't enter simply because they don't recognise quality," Smith said, noting the country had only two quality grades, the higher of which was sometimes not very good.
Smith acknowledged some cattle producers had concerns about international pacts such as NAFTA and GATT but said "the future of agriculture in America is in open markets around the world."
"We know we can compete with any country if you take away the trade barriers and the subsidies," he said.
Smith and other members of the House Agriculture Committee visited Argentina and Chile to assess the impact on agriculture of the two countries joining NAFTA.
